Class ConfigurableTextEffect

java.lang.Object
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.ConfigurableTextEffect
All Implemented Interfaces:
IChromaticEffect
Direct Known Subclasses:
BreathEffect, ChromaGlitchEffect, ChromaWaveEffect, CompressEffect, CustomItalicEffect, DiscordGradientEffect, DynamicEffect, GlitchEffect, GradientEffect, LetterSpacingEffect, LiquidPlasmaEffect, MatrixRainEffect, MatrixSpinEffect, MirroredGradientEffect, PhoenixEffect, PulseEffect, RainbowWaveEffect, ScaleEffect, ShiverEffect, StaticRainbowEffect, StretchEffect, TextOutlineEffect, VerticalGradientEffect, VerticalShearEffect, Volumetric3DEffect, WobbleEffect, WordFadeEffect
public abstract class ConfigurableTextEffect extends Object implements IChromaticEffect
Defines the supported options and validation rules for built-in effects.

Each effect exposes only the keys appropriate to its class. A rule describes a value's type, bounds and units; the effect's own formula supplies the default when the key is absent. For example, amplitudeY is a distance in GUI pixels, while opacity is a fraction.

The movement factory configures a fresh effect before returning it. Validation builds a separate map first, then stores immutable option/palette copies. Callbacks read those stored values without disk access. This object has no locking for concurrent reconfiguration: finish construction before sharing it through a definition snapshot.

  • Method Details

    • parameters

      public final Map<String, ConfigurableTextEffect.Parameter> parameters()
      Lists the option names, value types, bounds and units supported by this effect.

      The factory applies additional checks when configuring the effect. For example, span and wavelength values must be greater than zero even though their rules list zero as the minimum. Related settings are checked together: fadeEnd must exceed fadeStart.

      Returns:
      unmodifiable option-to-rule map, including only keys accepted by this class
